b: I'm 28 and have tried starting a few small ventures. Some made me just enough money to get by, while others never made it past the planning stage because the initial investment scared me off.
I started a one-year university certificate in management partly because I wanted to build the confidence to eventually start something of my own.
I've always felt like entrepreneurship was my calling. I constantly listen to business podcasts, read business books, and genuinely love talking about business.
The problem is that whenever I come up with an idea, I get scared when it's time to put money on the line. I end up doing a lot of talking and planning, but not nearly enough doing.

For those of you who took the leap and started something, how did you find the confidence to do it? Did it come naturally, or was there something that helped you overcome the fear and take that first risk?
